PhunkyPhil 2026/11/10 02:16
I don't have any evidence/study to substantiate this but I have the feeling there's a _massive_ amount of fiddling with the quant/functionality of the models at different stages of the release cycle and account freshness.

Every time a new model drops it feels wildly powerful, then regresses to some sort of generic SOTA level we've been used to over the last 6 months.

I remember my first coding prompt with, I think it was sonnet 4.6, on a fresh account and it was shocking how much it successfully did off a single prompt - I haven't found that with any other model at any other time and I suspect it was because they put me at the top of the priority list to get a "wow" reaction.

Regression after a release is pretty well-agreed upon, but I'm wondering if they secretly have a huge amount in the tank they aren't releasing. Either as a card to play in the future, or because they can't keep up with demand. I've heard anecdotes of people working in these companies saying that the public models aren't even close to their actual capabilities... Anyone have any opinion on this?

nickalaso 2026/11/10 02:53
So, IMO, they have much better capability internally because they have 'unlimited' usage. I also suspect a lot of 'Fable' is just a shit ton of nested subagents doing necessary backend work with a very solid fine tuned LLM conversing with the user.

I worked recently for a German megacorp, for whatever reason they gave us unlimited access to a bunch of models, up to sonnet 4.5/Gpt o1 etc, so not the best or latest models. And no agentic tools.

So I built a custom Claude Code clone because they exposed the api from their custom 'LLM Chat' clone in the client and accepted my user credentials for access.

Essentially a frankenstein AI harness using various models for their strengths, including using the OpenAI best model for memory context consolidation and compaction + Sonnet as orchestrator, etc. I was able to spawn 20+ agents to do my work and basically automate my entire job at that corp. I think my internal bill was something like 5k euros per month and I was being careful to not abuse it...

It was better than the best you could get from claude at the time (about a year ago now I think), in terms of task performance completion.

So imagine what someone with essentially infinite spend can do with endless fable agents. AKA US government and Anthropic internal.

mrinterweb 2026/11/10 03:44
The thing that bothers me is the false advertising. The models are announced with specific capabilities and benchmark scores. Then they silently nerf the models after release. Without a public acknowledgement that a production model has been nerfed and what the new benchmarks are, people are assuming the model has the original capabilities. People are choosing to pay for models based on their reported capabilities. Customers trust these models to deliver the reported capability. It feels like false advertising to me when they say one thing and deliver something less silently hoping no one finds out.

If I order a 16oz beer and get a 12oz pour, I'm going to call it out.
